name: RSS Guard
description: Downloads a Windows installer via GitHub Releases API and ShellExecutes it — no hash/signature. TLS on, but disable-TLS dead code sits commented-out in the same file.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

original_evidence.text: | RSSGuard | github.com/martinrotter/rssguard | C++/Qt (native) | Y | **platform-dependent**: on Windows = auto-chk + manual-dl/inst (checks on startup automatically if enabled, but download/install of the chosen installer requires the user to click "Download"/"Install" in the FormUpdate dialog); on macOS/Linux = notify/manual only (self-update unsupported, dialog just offers "Go to application website") | **Y (Windows only)** | https — `RELEASES_LIST = "https://api.github.com/repos/martinrotter/rssguard/releases"`; installer asset fetched from GitHub's `browser_download_url` (also https, github release CDN). TLS-bypass code (`ssl_conf.setPeerVerifyMode(QSslSocket::PeerVerifyMode::VerifyNone)` and `reply->ignoreSslErrors(error)`) **exists in source but is commented out / dead code**, so validation=enforced (default Qt/OS TLS trust store; the bypass is present-but-inactive) | HTTPS-only (GitHub Releases API JSON; no separate signed manifest — the "manifest" is just the GitHub releases JSON array, integrity relies on TLS to api.github.com) | none — no hash or signature check performed on the downloaded installer in-app; on Windows it's saved to a temp dir and launched directly via `ShellExecute`; any protection would come solely from the executable's own OS code-signing (if present) being honored by Windows SmartScreen/AppLocker outside the app's control | server-TLS only (no in-app payload verification); OS-code-signing check, if any, is external to the app | src/librssguard/miscellaneous/systemfactory.h:51-52,89 and .cpp:435-478 (`checkForUpdates`, `checkForUpdatesOnStartup`, JSON parse of GitHub releases); src/librssguard/definitions/definitions.h:67 (`RELEASES_LIST` URL); src/librssguard/gui/dialogs/formupdate.cpp:221-260 (Windows-only `ShellExecute` launch of downloaded installer, no hash/signature check, `#if defined(Q_OS_WIN)` gates self-update); src/librssguard/network-web/basenetworkaccessmanager.cpp:64-67,117-124 (SSL-bypass code present but commented out) |

| RSS Guard | **C** | Downloads + `ShellExecute`s an unsigned, unhashed Windows installer fetched over HTTPS from a GitHub-Releases-API-discovered URL. Nothing stops a compromised/forged GitHub release or a MITM with a valid cert for the download host from achieving RCE. Dead code (commented out) that would disable TLS verification is a latent-risk flag. |
